response.rationale: The vignette describes an expansile, mildly enhancing soft-tissue mass in the anterosuperior nasal cavity encroaching on the left orbital cavity, with extension to the cribriform plate, and a cystic mass occupying the left fronto-ethmoid region with destruction of the anterior skull base. These findings are strongly supportive of Esthesioneuroblastoma (D2). While Inverted Papilloma (D4) also has some supporting features, the aggressive nature of the mass with orbital involvement and skull base destruction makes Esthesioneuroblastoma a more fitting diagnosis.
